analysis.title: The biggest buyer on wall street is about to hit the buy button
key_insights: Corporate buybacks have been unusually quiet during the earnings blackout, and the buyback window is reopening. The note calls corporate repurchases one of the biggest structural buyers of US equities.
Goldman estimates 12% of S&P 500 companies are currently in an open buyback window, with another 22% exiting blackout by the end of the week.
October buyback activity has been running roughly 40% below the YTD average. As blackout restrictions lift, the note expects corporate demand to move back toward normal levels.
2026 YTD repurchase authorizations have reached a record $1.305 trillion, up from $1.151 trillion in 2025, per Goldman's buyback desk.
S&P 500 gross buybacks grew 15% y/y in H1 2026, with growth accelerating to 20% in Q2, so the trend was strengthening before the latest blackout.
Goldman expects US equity issuance to be less than 1% of Russell 3000 market capitalization in 2027, so new supply is limited.
Only five new repurchase programs totalling $2 billion were announced last week. The note expects news flow to pick up significantly over the next few days, with some major new authorizations.
The note's conclusion is that the corporate bid is about to get stronger regardless of the macro narrative.
earnings_insights: Earnings blackout windows are ending: 12% of S&P 500 companies are in an open buyback window now and another 22% exit blackout by the end of the week (Goldman estimate).
vol_and_positioning: Corporate buyback activity in October ran roughly 40% below the YTD average during blackout. The note expects it to rebound toward normal as windows reopen.
Record $1.305 trillion of 2026 YTD buyback authorizations and limited new equity issuance (under 1% of Russell 3000 market cap expected in 2027) are cited as a supportive technical bid.
